title: Stale Signal
subtitle: A Telemetry Outage, a Transmission-Main Break and a Boil-Water Decision

brief.userPrompt: During a July heat wave with demand near 14 MGD the Hilltop Tank radio repeater RP-1 fails at 05:30, so Orchard Standpipe, Northgate and Mill Road telemetry go stale on the HMI and the operators acknowledge the stale-data flags; at 06:10 the 24-inch Hilltop Transmission Main breaks near Summit Drive and Hilltop Tank begins to drain with no remote levels visible. Isolation valves V-2410 and V-2418, Mill Road Booster Station, the Carver County Water District interconnect IC-1, pressure at Millbrook General Hospital, and the boil-water decision for the depressurized part of Zone 2.
constraints: Every email address of the City and the department uses the exercise domain millbrook-oh.example; outside parties use fictional domains and the fictional outlets of the communications plan (Channel 4, the Millbrook Courier); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (Carver County Water District, Millbrook General Hospital, Ohio EPA DDAGW, the Carver County Health Commissioner, the media) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Running blind: a main break during a telemetry outage, the hydraulics of isolation in a heat wave, and a boil-water decision without pressure data
overview.threat: On the third day of a July heat wave, with demand near 14 MGD, the 24 VDC power supply in the Hilltop Tank radio cabinet fails at 05:30. It feeds both the repeater RP-1 and the cellular modem of RTU-01, so Hilltop Tank, Orchard Standpipe, the Orchard Wellfield, Northgate and Mill Road Booster Station all go stale on the HMI at once. At 06:10 the 1968 cast-iron, 24-inch Hilltop Transmission Main breaks near Summit Drive. Hilltop Tank starts to drain, and nobody at the plant can see it.
overview.operationalImpact: The break first shows at the plant as a jump in FIT-501 and a fall in PIT-501, then in calls from Summit Drive. Isolation needs valves V-2410 and V-2418, and V-2418 was last exercised in 2023. Holding Zone 2 means starting Mill Road Booster Station, which draws on Zone 1, where Millbrook General Hospital has no storage, and probably opening the Carver County Water District interconnect IC-1, whose chloraminated water matters to dialysis patients. Part of Zone 2 falls below 20 psi, which triggers the advisory decision in ERP 7.1, but with the telemetry down nobody knows exactly which streets. Northgate Reservoir, filled from Zone 2, starts to fall too.

overview.targetAudience: Water Operations, Distribution, SCADA / IT, Water Quality / Lab, Public Information
overview.location: Riverside Water Treatment Plant, 1400 River Road, Millbrook, Carver County, Ohio

objectives.name: Telemetry Trust
objectives.text: Keep the Control Room, the field crews, the lab and the PIO on one picture of the system while the HMI shows stale data, using radio DWS-1, field readings every two hours and the OT Plan 10.6 checklist.

objectives.name: Zone Isolation
objectives.text: Decide, from incomplete pressure data, the area and timing of a Boil Water Advisory for the depressurized part of Zone 2 (ERP 7.1 and 9), and whether and when to open IC-1.

objectives.name: Boil Water Decision
objectives.text: Recognize the main-break signature (ERP 6.6), isolate the break with the fewest valves, and manage the hydraulic trade-offs between Zone 2, Zone 1 and Zone 3.

objectives.name: Inter-Team Coordination
objectives.text: Follow ERP 7.1, the OT Plan 10.6 stale-data checklist, the ERP 9.5 notification sequence and the DDAGW consultation, with critical customers called before the public.

roles.name: Director of Water Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Commands the response: declares the incident level, approves isolation, booster and interconnect operations, and decides on advisories with the Water Quality Manager.
standingOrders: A stale value is unknown, not the last good value.

For a Hilltop Transmission Main break: start Mill Road Booster Station and run the Orchard Wellfield at full capacity; request IC-1 if Zone 2 demand exceeds about 7 MGD or Hilltop Tank falls below 12 ft (ERP 7.1).
If pressure anywhere fell below 20 psi, start the advisory decision before repairs are complete.
Zone 1 has no storage: warn the hospital at once if Zone 1 pressure is at risk.

roles.name: SCADA / IT Security Manager (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns control-system integrity, remote access, and evidence preservation; investigates telemetry failure and confirms no cyber compromise.
standingOrders: Find out whether a telemetry outage is the radio, the gateway or a server (OT Plan 10.6).
A telemetry outage during an unusual flow or pressure trend is CODE CLEARWATER until explained.
List every stale tag with its last update time before acknowledging the alarm.
Restore telemetry with the parts and people available; record what was replaced.

roles.name: Public Information Officer (PIO)
roles.description: Owns public messaging, social media, press, and the MillbrookAlert system; releases advisories and updates.
standingOrders: Critical customers (hospital, dialysis, Summit Care) hear from DWS before the public.
Describe advisory areas by streets from the map of record, never by neighborhood names alone.
Give a time for the next update every time.
A Boil Water Advisory says boil one minute for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and ice; bathing is fine.

roles.name: Water Quality Manager (Compliance)
roles.description: Owns sampling, lab results, regulatory reporting, and public-notice triggers; confirms loss of disinfection and lifting criteria.
standingOrders: Pressure below 20 psi or customers out of water starts the advisory decision and the ERP-3 sampling.
Sample the depressurized area and the first hydrants on its edge; coliform takes 18–24 hours.
Consult DDAGW within 24 hours of a Tier 1 situation.
Recommend lifting only after pressure has held above 20 psi for 24 hours and two rounds of samples 24 hours apart are satisfactory.

roles.name: Distribution Superintendent (Distribution)
roles.description: Owns the distribution system: main breaks, valves, interconnects IC-1 and IC-2, boosters in the field, flushing, door hangers and field pressure readings.
standingOrders: Isolate a break with the fewest valves and confirm the isolated area by street (ERP 7.1).
IC-1 is a two-person valve operation after a phone call to the Carver County Water District duty desk.
Read storage sites by sight gauge every two hours while telemetry is stale (OT Plan 10.6).
Flush, disinfect and sample a repaired main before it returns to service.

phases.title: Stale Signal
phases.goal: Work out what the stale flags hide and recognize a main break from the plant’s own instruments and the first calls.
beats: At 05:35 the HMI shows stale data from Hilltop Tank, Orchard Standpipe, the wellfield, Northgate and Mill Road at once; Eastfield (cellular) still reports.
At 05:50 Buckeye Telemetry says no technician can arrive before 10:00 and asks whether the shared 24 VDC supply in the RP-1 cabinet is alive.
At 06:12 FIT-501 jumps and PIT-501 falls at the plant: the main-break signature in ERP 6.6.
At 06:20 Customer Service has calls from Summit Drive about water coming up through the pavement; at 06:25 the crew at Hilltop Tank reads the sight gauge falling fast.

phases.title: Isolation
phases.goal: Confirm and isolate the break while protecting Zone 1 pressure and the hospital, and get telemetry back.
beats: At 06:35 the crew confirms the 24-inch break at Summit Drive and heads for V-2410 and V-2418.
At 06:45 Millbrook General Hospital reports its supply pressure falling as the plant pushes water out of the break.
At 06:55 the SCADA technician finds the failed power supply; a spare is in the Distribution shop.
At 07:15 Channel 4 has video of the geyser on Summit Drive and asks if the water is safe.

phases.title: Boil-Water Decision
phases.goal: Decide the advisory area from partial data and decide on IC-1, with Hilltop Tank still falling.
beats: At 07:30 Hilltop Tank reads about 21 ft by sight gauge and the break is still running.
At 07:55 the Health Commissioner asks for the advisory area: the whole zone or the streets that lost pressure? This is the decision point.
At 08:05 V-2410 is closed but V-2418 will not turn.
At 08:15 the Carver County Water District offers IC-1 within the hour; at 08:25 telemetry returns and shows Zone 1 suction near the booster lockout.

phases.title: Holding Two Zones
phases.goal: Hold Zone 2 and Zone 3 with the boosters and the interconnect, sample the depressurized area and keep the public informed.
beats: At 08:35 BP-401 trips on low suction; at 08:45 the first grab samples in the depressurized area show low residual.
At 08:55 the Deputy PIO’s draft notice needs correcting; at 09:05 Northgate Reservoir is found falling because ALV-301 has nothing to fill from.
At 09:15 the Millbrook Courier asks about the 1968 main; at 09:25 DDAGW records the Tier 1 consultation.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 05:30 on Tuesday, July 14, the third day of a heat wave. Demand is near 14 MGD and the forecast high is 97°F. The plant is in automatic with one operator in the RWTP Control Room; the day shift arrives at 06:00. Hilltop Tank reads 33 ft after the overnight fill. No alarms are active.
msel.expectedAction: Each team states its heat-wave staffing and what it watches first in the morning peak.

msel.event: System Log: At 05:30 MBW-HMI-01 flags RTU-02 (Orchard Standpipe), RTU-03 (Northgate), RTU-04 (Mill Road Booster Station) and RTU-06 (Orchard Wellfield) as STALE. RTU-01 (Hilltop Tank) should have failed over to cellular but is stale too; its last good level was 33.1 ft at 05:29. RTU-05 (Eastfield, cellular) and RTU-07 (Intake) are reporting.
msel.expectedAction: The SCADA / IT Security Manager lists every stale tag with its last update time before the alarm is acknowledged (OT Plan 10.6) and asks why RTU-01’s cellular failover did not work; the IC sends Distribution to Hilltop Tank first and orders sight-gauge readings every two hours.

metrics.name: Detection Without Telemetry
metrics.fail: Stale values were treated as current, or the main break was not recognized until crews reported it from the street.
metrics.pass: Stale tags were listed and Hilltop Tank checked by sight gauge after I-01; the break was named from the plant signature at I-05.
metrics.excellence: The team linked I-01, I-02 and I-09 to a single power supply, closed the cyber question quickly and kept two-hour field readings going until 08:20.

metrics.name: Isolation and Hydraulics
metrics.fail: Mill Road Booster Station was run without regard to Zone 1 suction; the hospital was not warned; IC-1 was opened without the dialysis notifications or not considered at all.
metrics.pass: The break was isolated with the fewest valves and the V-2418 problem handled by I-15; the hospital was warned at I-08; IC-1 was requested against the ERP 7.1 triggers with dialysis patients told first.
metrics.excellence: The team anticipated the BP-401 lockout before I-18b and the Northgate drawdown before I-21, and set trigger levels for each.

metrics.name: Advisory Decision
metrics.fail: No advisory decision was made, or one was made without DDAGW, Public Health, the City Manager’s approval or an ERP-2 record.
metrics.pass: At I-14 the Director and the Water Quality Manager decided the area with DDAGW and Public Health, recorded the basis on ERP-2 and called critical customers before release.
metrics.excellence: The area was drawn by streets and widened as I-17 and I-19 came in, and the PIO was given a realistic lifting time from the DDAGW criteria.

metrics.name: Public Information
metrics.fail: An advisory was announced before it was decided, or the I-20 draft went out with the wrong area or instructions.
metrics.pass: The PIO answered I-11 and I-12b with facts and next-update times and corrected the I-20 draft before release.
metrics.excellence: Notices used street boundaries and standard boil-water instructions, and the I-22 capital question was deferred without speculation.

hotwash.methodDescription: Each team names three things that went well and three that did not; the facilitator writes them up and looks for the same issue in more than one team.

questions.text: How did you keep a picture of Zone 2 while the HMI showed stale data, and when did you first say “main break”?
When did the team see that starting Mill Road Booster Station would pull down Zone 1 and the hospital? What did you do about it?
How did you decide the boil-water area without pressure data, and what would have made you widen or shrink it?
When did you open IC-1, and who told the dialysis patients about chloramine before it reached them?
One 24-volt supply took out five sites and the failover. What goes in the after-action report?

simcellScripts.trigger: A player orders a valve closed, a booster started or a reading taken.
hardQuestions: Which valve first, and who goes to V-2418 with the machine?
If we close V-2422 instead, who calls the 1,800 extra customers?
Do you want us reading Hilltop every 30 minutes or every two hours?
concessions: Carry out any order that names the valve or site and the reason.

simcellScripts.trigger: DWS calls the hospital, or no one has by 07:00.
hardQuestions: Do I switch to tanker now? I need four hours’ notice and it costs us.
What is my pressure going to be at noon?
concessions: Holds on stored water and prepares the tanker switch once given a time for the next call.

simcellScripts.trigger: The IC asks for approval of an advisory over 5,000 people.
hardQuestions: Why the whole zone — or why not the whole zone?
How long will it last, and when does Summit Drive reopen?
concessions: Approves the advisory once told the area by streets, the basis and the lifting criteria.

warnings.message: The Hilltop Tank repeater RP-1 failure is not confirmed in C1; the documents state it is a 900 MHz radio to plant and repeater, not a standalone repeater. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Change 'Hilltop Tank radio repeater RP-1' to 'Hilltop Tank RTU-01 (900 MHz radio to plant and repeater)' to match C4.

warnings.message: The Mill Road Booster Station is not a pump station; the documents list it as 'Mill Road Booster Station' with pumps BP-401 and BP-402, not 'Mill Road Booster'. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Correct 'Mill Road Booster Station' to 'Mill Road Booster Station' and remove 'Booster' from the name to match C4.

warnings.message: The manual isolation valves V-2410 and V-2418 are not listed in C1; the documents do not reference any such valves.
warnings.suggestion: Replace V-2410 and V-2418 with 'the isolation point at the Hilltop Transmission Main near Summit Drive' to match C1.

warnings.message: The inject in I-11 is in the voice of the Director of Water Operations (Incident Commander), which violates inject hygiene (5b). (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Rewrite I-11 as a phone call from an external agency (e.g., Ohio EPA) or a formal directive from the City Manager, not a player role.

warnings.message: The inject in I-23 is in the voice of the Director of Water Operations (Incident Commander), which violates inject hygiene (5b). (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Rewrite I-23 as a phone call from the Ohio EPA DDAGW or a formal report from the City Manager, not a player role.

warnings.message: The business network isolation is not supported by C5; the documents state that the business network is not isolated by CISA or FBI guidance.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the CISA and FBI guidance reference and instead state that the business network is isolated due to a simulated ransomware attack on the IT server.

warnings.message: The roof hatch switch ZS-601 is not listed in C4; the documents state it is 'roof hatch switch ZS-601' but not as a triggerable event.
warnings.suggestion: Change 'ZS-601 was triggered' to 'ZS-601 was found in the open position' to match C4.

warnings.message: The IC-1 meter FIT-631 shows 2.5 MGD, but the documents state that IC-1 is a normally closed valve and no flow is expected until opened.
warnings.suggestion: Change 'FIT-631 shows 2.5 MGD' to 'FIT-631 shows 0.0 MGD' until IC-1 is confirmed open.

warnings.message: The Northgate Booster Station RTU-03 is not listed in C4; the documents state it is RTU-03 but not as a site with a VFD lockout.
warnings.suggestion: Replace 'VFDs have locked out' with 'the site is now in manual mode' to match C4.

warnings.message: The PLC-02 backup missing is not supported by C2; the documents state that Kessler Controls windows are manually disabled and logged, not that backups are missing.
warnings.suggestion: Replace the missing backup claim with a Kessler Controls window that was not properly closed, leading to unauthorized access.

warnings.message: The inject in I-01 lacks a 'from' field; it must be assigned to an external party. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Assign the System Alert to 'Facilitator' and add a 'from' field to match inject hygiene (5b).
